citations.F1: Fix the N+1: `serialize_event` issues one `SELECT ... FROM users` per event — 1,000 sequential round-trips per request — either join `users` into the main query or batch with `WHERE id = ANY($1)`.
citations.F2: the dedupe uses `seen` as a list, so membership is a linear scan — O(n²); make it a set
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` uses blocking `requests.get` (2 s timeout) inside an async handler, so every cache miss parks the whole event loop ... switch to an async client
citations.F4: Add `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_org_created_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)` — the only indexes today are on `actor_id` and `kind`, so the query scans all 4.2 M rows
citations.F5: `_request_timings` is an unbounded list appended on every request by the middleware ... replace it with a fixed-size ring buffer or a bucketed histogram
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` is an unbounded dict keyed on client IP with no eviction — bound it with an LRU and a TTL
citations.F7: Verify with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` on acme's parameters before and after step 7, then re-measure p95 for org 4127
citations.F9: 16 workers × 50 connections × 6 pods = 4,800 Postgres connections against a default `max_connections` of 100 — that takes the database down ... If latency is still unacceptable after 7, 8, and 10, then consider caching
citations.F11: the Redis cache would never hit: `since` defaults to `datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=30)`, a distinct value on every request, so every key is unique
